1466.name: Travis Kelce

brief.prose: The unquestioned Chiefs starter at 36 in Year 14, but Andy Reid is openly managing his practice reps, a rotation about age rather than a demotion. Kelce came back focused after mulling retirement and Reid says he is 'playing like crazy,' though last year's drops resurfaced. In a shallow-TE format he's still a startable TE1 on name and red-zone role, but age-driven decline, drops and target erosion behind Mahomes' younger receivers make him a fading, floor-questionable starter you shouldn't pay a premium for. Startable, not a difference-maker.
brief.rationale: Locked but declining TE1; startable in a shallow-TE format on role and name, but fading volume makes him a no-premium play.

At 33 the role is secure; the ceiling shrinks with Nacua back.

At 33, availability is the cap, and Friday's designation decides Week 4.

Doyle stopped short of promising 300+ carries for a third straight year but committed directly to 'an immense role' and 'a pretty large workload,' and Henry himself is chasing rushing-yardage milestones (994 yards from 6th all-time) that keep him fully bought in. A locked, elite bell-cow with massive goal-line and rushing-TD volume (6-point TDs); half-PPR receiving stays minimal but the touchdown and yardage floor is elite. A set-and-forget RB1 whose only cap is age-driven regression.

4034.name: Christian McCaffrey
4034.adp_commentary: Market drafts him ~RB5 (ADP 5.7) while the board values him ~RB9. You're paying up for ceiling against an age-30, Achilles-history availability cap. A slight reach at cost in a format where RB-adjacent value is available later.

availability.history: 2024 lost 13 games to bilateral Achilles tendinitis (soft-tissue, both legs) + late PCL sprain; answered with a 17-game RB1 season in 2025. Age 30 + Achilles history is the recurrence/decline risk, not a current injury.

brief.prose: San Francisco is rotating McCaffrey on purpose. In Week 1 he played 36 snaps and carried 10 times to rookie Kaelon Black's 14, and OC Klay Kubiak said the goal was to spare him and "get Kaelon touches." Week 2 at home against Miami pointed back the other way on volume: McCaffrey carried 10 times for 23 yards and two touchdowns and added four catches for 43 yards, while Black (groin, active as expected) had 7 carries for 25 and Jordan James 4 for 15, in a 35-13 win where the whole run game managed 63 yards. That is a three-back rotation with McCaffrey keeping the lead share and the passing-game role, and no evidence yet that Black's Week 1 carry edge was more than a one-week game script. Watch whether Black's carry share holds in a game the 49ers do not lead early.
brief.rationale: The coordinator described a deliberate lighter load and Week 2 showed a real three-back split, but McCaffrey led carries, scored twice and kept the receiving work, so the rotation is confirmed and the size of Black's share is still open.

5850.name: Josh Jacobs
5850.adp_commentary: RB at ~25.2. Top-12 RB talent, but a pending domestic-violence case (felony charge, undecided) plus a 2025 knee that sapped his second half make this a genuine avoid-until-clarity at cost. The ADP has not fully absorbed the legal risk.

availability.history: 2025 knee (missed Weeks 11-12; noticeably less effective after: 14.6 touches/11.3 pts vs 21.1/19.6 before).

brief.prose: The legal-outcome bet resolved into a confirmed absence, not a pending risk: the NFL placed Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List on Aug. 30, which bars him from practicing or playing in any capacity for as long as he's on it, three days after Brown County formally charged him with two misdemeanors (battery, criminal damage to property) tied to the May domestic incident. GM Brian Gutekunst has said a suspension could still follow once the NFL's own conduct review concludes, meaning the exempt-list stint may only be the front end of a longer absence rather than the whole of it, with no set timeline either way. Green Bay hedged the same day, trading a 2028 sixth-round pick for Steelers RB Kaleb Johnson to sit behind newly-elevated starter MarShawn Lloyd (5 of 7 snaps on Green Bay's preseason opening drive, plus a touchdown). Jacobs remains the clean zone-scheme fit in LaFleur/Stenavich's offense whenever he is eligible to return, but Lloyd, not Jacobs, is Green Bay's playable back for the foreseeable future.
brief.rationale: Confirmed Commissioner's-Exempt placement (not just a pending charge) makes this a real, current zero with no return timeline — a bigger and more certain role delta than the Aug. 28 brief priced in.

His earliest eligible return is Week 6 (Oct. 18 vs. NYJ), with Week 8 vs. Miami the more realistic target. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams move up as the WR corps in his absence (Kayshon Boutte, previously the WR3, was traded to Houston in late August and is no longer part of this room). The role case for Brown himself is unchanged and locked once healthy; the only variable is the calendar.

Dowdle (toe) did not practice at all this week and Pittsburgh ruled him out Wednesday for the Thursday night game against the Browns, his second straight missed game. In Week 3 without him Jaylen Warren played 90% of the snaps and ran 17 times for 127 yards with three catches for 31 yards. CB Joey Porter Jr. is also out.
events.so_what: Settled before Thursday kickoff: bench Dowdle and start Warren at RB or FLEX as a near-every-down back again. Dowdle stays a bench hold; nothing points to IR.

brief.prose: O'Connell's retooled wide-zone run scheme looks built for Mason's burst and vision; The Athletic's Alec Lewis wrote the new concepts fit him 'perfectly.' Wes Phillips said Mason 'dropped some pounds' and O'Connell called him 'in unbelievable shape,' with camp reports showing him outproducing Jones in team drills. Both backs remain listed as co-starters, but building sentiment trends toward Mason as the 1a. If that holds, an early-down, between-the-tackles lead in this scheme is real RB2 value (goal-line 6-point TDs help); half-PPR caps him slightly since Jones keeps the passing-down role, but a rising 1a at this ADP is a live value.
brief.rationale: Ascending 1a in a scheme built for him; real RB2 upside with goal-line TD value, lightly capped in half-PPR by Jones's passing role.

9221.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
9221.adp_commentary: RB2 at ~2.9. Campbell's 'bell cow now' comments consolidate his touches (the single most valuable RB signal in this format), so a top-3 price is correct.

availability.history: Minor 2023 (15 games), 17/17 since. No chronic pattern.

brief.prose: Detroit made him the highest-paid running back in NFL history this offseason and Dan Campbell has called him the 'bell cow now' behind a run-heavy scheme fit under new OC Drew Petzing. That bell-cow read got reinforced Sept. 1 when Detroit placed backup Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve (back injury, after an earlier MCL sprain had already healed) for a minimum of four games; Pacheco was the only proven complementary back in the room after Detroit traded David Montgomery to Houston, so his absence removes what little committee risk existed and pushes even more early-down and short-yardage work Gibbs' way. No clear backup has emerged yet from what's left of the depth chart. Coming off 1,223 rushing yards, 18 total TDs, and 616 receiving yards in 2025, this remains a true three-down workhorse projection with the roster context now pointing further toward, not away from, a monster workload.
brief.rationale: Pacheco's IR stint removes Detroit's only proven backup, reinforcing rather than changing the existing bell-cow projection.

9224.name: Chase Brown
9224.adp_commentary: RB at ~19.1. One of the board's biggest RB values vs ADP. CIN volume + a clean recent workload make him a target a full round after his value rank.

availability.history: 2023 rookie limited (12 games); 16/17 since. Trending durable.

brief.prose: Locked atop Cincinnati's backfield in a contract year behind a line returning all five starters, and camp reports have only deepened the role: Brown told reporters this week Pitcher is 'putting me in the slot, and allowing me to use my full skill set to make plays,' on top of Burrow calling him a 'close second' to Chase for touches. Only Perine and Tahj Brooks sit behind him, and he's shown no health issues beyond a single illness-related absence. The half-PPR receiving work, 6-point TD scoring, and now a widened route-running role stack a high floor under real ceiling upside. A strong RB1.
brief.rationale: Locked lead back with an expanding slot/receiving role confirmed by his own quotes this week, no health flags; a high-floor RB1 with route-running upside.

brief.prose: Young remains the unchallenged starter, and new full-time playcaller Brad Idzik (taking over from Canales, who called plays the past two years) has specifically praised Young's growing command of the pre-snap process, crediting him as a driving force behind the offense. Idzik has no NFL play-calling track record outside the preseason, so the passing shape that produced Young's career-best 2025 (3,011 yards, 23 TDs) is now being run by a first-timer, a real variance factor in a 4-pt-pass-TD format that needs consistent volume to pay off.
brief.rationale: Job security isn't in question, but the first-time playcaller is a genuine unknown, not clearly a mispriced upside or downside case yet.

9484.name: Tucker Kraft
9484.adp_commentary: TE at ~68. An ascending GB TE; the 2025 games-missed is the availability question. A mid-round TE dart with real upside if healthy.

availability.history: 2025 missed time (8 games); cause not separately verified this pass. Flagged for re-check.

brief.prose: Kraft has moved fully past his ACL recovery this camp. He took a full-speed hit in the Aug. 26 joint practice against Arizona and called it confirmation he's ready for real contact, then said the next day he's off any rep count entirely: 'I'm not doing the rep count stuff anymore... I'm gonna try to be out there as much as I can.' He's sitting out only the meaningless preseason finale, with the Sept. 13 opener at Minnesota the actual target. Green Bay's Aug. 27 signing of veteran Jonnu Smith is insurance for backup Luke Musgrave's neck injury, not a hedge on Kraft's own health. Still the same YAC-heavy red-zone weapon when right, and the health picture now reads clean rather than ramping.
brief.rationale: Off the rep count entirely and took a live hit clean in the Aug. 26-27 joint-practice window; the Jonnu Smith signing addresses Musgrave's injury, not Kraft's.

brief.prose: Jacksonville's first unofficial depth chart lists Washington as the top man on one outside receiver spot, with Brian Thomas Jr. on the other and Jakobi Meyers in the slot. Travis Hunter is a two-way piece but his snaps are trending hard to defense (116 of 178 reps on defense through Aug. 20), which clears true boundary volume for Washington rather than a three-way timeshare. Coen's staff has praised his route consistency. With Hunter mostly on defense, Washington projects as a near-full-time boundary starter, giving him real half-PPR sleeper appeal at a WR-dart price; the role is emerging rather than locked, so an upside bench WR worth a late look.
brief.rationale: Emerging near-full-time boundary starter as Hunter shifts to defense; a real half-PPR sleeper at a WR-dart ADP, upside more than locked.

9488.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
9488.adp_commentary: WR2 at ~7.3. Led the NFL with ~44% of Seattle's air yards in 2025, format-correct here (yardage-driven, survives half-PPR). The pick your team name already endorses.

brief.prose: The featured receiver in Seattle's passing game by a wide margin: a 37.9% target share through three games, the highest in the NFL, with 36 targets, 27 catches, 405 yards and six touchdowns, and Next Gen Stats show most of his Week 3 work (12 of 14 targets, both scores) came lined up out wide rather than in the slot. Sam Darnold returned in Week 3 and hit him for 10-128-2 against Washington. Mike Macdonald shrugged off the concentration question, saying the ball will find other players at some point, so some regression in share is the watch item, but no teammate (Cooper Kupp, Rashid Shaheed, Tory Horton, AJ Barner) is close to challenging the role.
brief.rationale: League-leading 37.9% target share with alignment versatility; Macdonald hints at spreading the ball, so the share is the only thing likely to drift.

9493.adp_commentary: WR at ~4.8. Elite when healthy; the PCL re-aggravation history plus Rams target competition cap an otherwise top-3 WR profile.

availability.history: 2024 PCL sprain (knee), re-aggravated from a joint practice, missed 6+; played 16 in 2025. Re-aggravation pattern is the watch.

brief.prose: When healthy the Rams run their offense through him first: they moved him into the slot on a career-high share of his routes after Davante Adams arrived, and he opened the season with 5 catches on 9 targets for 74 yards against the 49ers. Groin soreness (McVay says it is unrelated to the psoas issue from camp) cost him Weeks 2 and 3, but he practiced on a limited basis Wednesday, his first session since Sept. 18, and McVay firmed up from 'hopeful' to saying he expects Nacua to play Sunday at Philadelphia. If he does, the target tree is narrow: TE Terrance Ferguson is likely out with an ankle sprain and Colby Parkinson has a shoulder issue. Watch whether he reaches a full practice by Friday.

The snaps are there (53 of 76 in the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati, up from 46% in his debut) but the targets are not: he caught 3 of 5 for 37 yards while Dalton Schultz drew 14 targets. Collins is expected to miss Week 3 against Indianapolis too, so the role lasts at least one more game, but it looks like a field-stretching, low-volume job that shrinks once Collins returns.

9509.name: Bijan Robinson
9509.adp_commentary: RB1 off the board at ~1.5. In a 2-RB/2-FLEX half-PPR league the elite bell-cow RB is the scarcest resource (top VORP tier), and Bijan's clean availability + workhorse role justify 1.01 cost despite Atlanta's stated wide-zone usage-cap talk.

brief.prose: Scheme fit stays locked: the gap- and power-run designs OC Tommy Rees layered onto Atlanta's outside-zone base, plus the league-leading screen package, are installed and Robinson is the hub of both. The one new wrinkle is Rees telling reporters Thursday he'd rather the offense be more balanced after Robinson's 29-touch, 21-of-31-run Week 1 workload, aiming to get Drake London and Kyle Pitts more involved. HC Kevin Stefanski backed a heavy plan regardless, saying of 29 touches a game, "I don't know. I think he wants to. That's what he's told me." A dial-back from an outlier 29-touch game toward a more normal 20-22 doesn't touch his bell-cow role or the screen-game usage that's his signature; Brian Robinson Jr. remains the only real committee threat.
brief.rationale: Rees's stated push for balance normalizes an outlier 29-touch game, not a threat to the underlying workhorse role or screen usage.

brief.prose: With Kenneth Walker III gone to Kansas City, Charbonnet is the presumptive lead back once healthy in new OC Brian Fleury's outside-zone scheme, a downhill style that suits him and builds in the receiving role. The catch is availability: he's rehabbing a Feb. 20 ACL surgery and remained on the active/PUP list as of Aug. 23. Macdonald says Week 1 is 'possible' but hasn't promised it, and with that late surgery date it's reasonable to expect him sidelined out of the gate, with interim touches defaulting to Jadarian Price and an unproven mix. Draft him for the lead-back upside once back, but discount a likely early-season absence, and note that staying on PUP through cuts would shelve him until Week 5.
brief.rationale: Lead-back upside once healthy, but a late ACL surgery leaves Week 1 a coin flip; a stash you discount for a probable early-season absence.

9756.adp_commentary: WR at ~98.4. The WR2 in a strong MIN passing game; the suspension is served and behind him. A steady value at cost, with the substance-policy history as a background note, not a live flag.

In half-PPR his WR2 target volume gives a steady floor, with boom weeks when coverage rolls to Jefferson the upside. A thumb knock has limited him in some team drills but reads as a minor monitor, not a role threat. A dependable WR3/flex with WR2 ceiling in a good offense.
brief.rationale: Locked MIN WR2 with steady half-PPR volume and spike-week upside off Jefferson coverage; the thumb is a minor monitor, not a role risk.

brief.prose: The improved camp has not survived contact with the season: Houston is 0-3 after a 19-17 loss to the previously winless Colts in which the offense managed 233 total yards and Stroud threw for 167. His own framing is blunt ("No excuses. No one cares about what happened") alongside "I believe we're not far off, but also it doesn't feel that way because we're 0-3," and he has pointedly kept the message on how Nick Caley uses personnel rather than on execution. The one real upgrade coming is Nico Collins, out two games with a hamstring and possibly back for Week 4 against Dallas, which matters because the receiver room thinned further when Jayden Higgins tore his ACL in August. He is still a pocket passer with no rushing floor in a league that pays 4 points for a passing touchdown, so even a Collins-fueled rebound leaves him a streamer rather than a starter.
brief.rationale: Locked starter on an 0-3 offense averaging under 250 yards a game, publicly pushing back on how the coordinator uses the personnel; Collins' return is the only upgrade in sight and the 4-point passing touchdown keeps the format ceiling low.

10229.name: Rashee Rice
10229.adp_commentary: WR at ~34.8 (~WR12). The ADP has already absorbed the jail stint and the knee. He's elite on the field, and the price IS the discount. A calculated-risk value if the knee clears camp; the conduct/legal history is documented but currently resolved.

availability.history: 2024 knee (LCL, 4 games) then a 2026 offseason knee clean-up (~2 months, debris removal). Verify the knee clears camp.

brief.prose: Rice keeps the exact role that made him a target-share monster: 28.7% team target share in 2025 as Mahomes' top underneath, high-YAC option. The legal cloud is now fully cleared for 2026: the domestic-violence investigation closed with no discipline, and having already served his 2025 six-game suspension for the car crash, he's available all season. He's cleared for full contact and says he's '100% locked in.' The cap is scheme, not health or availability: a 4.7-yard career aDOT makes his ceiling volume-driven, so treat him as a high-floor PPR target hog rather than a big-play WR1.
brief.rationale: Cleared for 2026 (no new suspension) and healthy; an elite-target-share PPR target hog with a high floor, capped only by a low aDOT.

A buy-the-bounce-back TE1 candidate.

10859.name: Sam LaPorta
10859.adp_commentary: TE at ~78. A healthy LaPorta is a top-5 TE, but a herniated disc is the kind of injury that lingers; the ADP is a fair midpoint between his ceiling and the back risk.

availability.history: Herniated disc in the back worsened in Nov 2025 → IR (9 games). Aiming to be fully cleared by camp; present read is Week 1, but back injuries can be tricky/recurrent.

brief.prose: Healthy and used the way Drew Petzing used Trey McBride, if not yet at that volume: 14 catches on 19 targets for 144 and a touchdown through three games on roughly two thirds of the snaps, with Week 3 a quiet 3-for-4 and 44 yards in the win over the Jets because Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs ate the targets. The Week 1 overtime win at New Orleans is the better look at why his snap share holds: five catches, 48 yards, and run blocking stout enough against Chase Young and Carl Granderson that Gibbs went for 154 at 5.4 a carry. Dan Campbell's read on his development is that the jump is in the run game and pass protection while he stays a pass-game threat, which is the version of this player who never leaves the field. The cap is the target queue in front of him, not the job.
brief.rationale: Healthy locked TE1 in a scheme that just produced the overall TE1; the ceiling is limited by St. Brown and Gibbs ahead of him in the target order rather than by any role risk.

brief.prose: The premise behind Wilson's price, that he's next in line for Zach Charbonnet's touches, doesn't match the camp pecking order: rookie Jadarian Price is the Week 1 starter, George Holani is the top backup, and Wilson sits third, with Charbonnet (ACL surgery in February) not expected back until the second half regardless. Macdonald has praised Wilson's flashes in camp, but new OC Fleury's stated plan to throw to running backs more plays to Holani's and Price's skill sets more than Wilson's, who offers little as a receiver, a real minus in this half-PPR format. He's a legitimate Week 1 roster-crunch risk, not a lead-back stash.
brief.rationale: Corrects a likely-mispriced assumption that Wilson is next-man-up for Charbonnet; camp reps put him third behind a rookie and Holani, and the new OC's pass-catching-back emphasis doesn't fit his skill set.

brief.prose: Williams is Chicago's franchise quarterback in Ben Johnson's offense, and he is ruled out for Week 3. He pulled up on a non-contact fourth-quarter scramble in the 9-3 loss to Minnesota; the MRI showed a low-grade hamstring strain with no tear, the team called him week-to-week, and he did not practice this week. The offense scored 13 points and leaned on its defense and on TreVeyon Henderson's 39-yard touchdown run. The role is locked; the August 'Brown clicking' case is on hold until he returns.

11566.name: Jayden Daniels
11566.adp_commentary: QB at ~64. A premium rushing-QB profile (the format's actual QB edge), but the 2025 games-missed needs verification before the draft; if healthy, a strong konami-code target that this league's QB-punters won't chase.

availability.history: 2025 missed significant time (7 games); cause not separately verified this pass. Flagged for the final-weeks re-check.

brief.prose: Health, not role, is the question. Daniels dislocated his left elbow in Week 2 at Dallas, his second dislocation of that elbow in ten months, and sat out Week 3; exams found no fracture and no significant ligament damage, so he avoided surgery and IR and will wear a protective brace. Dan Quinn says he travels to London and practices in some form this week, with Wednesday a walkthrough and Thursday the real test before a decision on Sunday against the Colts. Marcus Mariota kept the offense functional in his absence (19 of 31, 183 yards, three TDs in the 33-31 upset of Seattle), so there is no pressure to rush him. When healthy the dual-threat role is intact; a brace and a repeat injury are reasons to expect a cautious return rather than a full rushing workload right away.
brief.rationale: Starter when healthy; left elbow dislocation (second in 10 months) with clean imaging, Week 4 status decided after Thursday practice in London.

events.headline: Jayden Daniels limited in London jog-through; Quinn has not ruled him out for Week 4
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 28 item. Daniels (dislocated left elbow) was listed as limited in Wednesday's jog-through in London, his first practice since the Week 2 injury. Dan Quinn called it a "good step," said Washington has not ruled him out against the Colts, and confirmed he will wear a brace on the left elbow for the rest of the season whenever he returns. Marcus Mariota threw three touchdowns in the Week 3 upset of Seattle.
events.so_what: Progress, not a clearance. A jog-through limited tag says little about game readiness; watch Thursday and Friday. 12527.adp_commentary: RB at ~11.9. Projected rookie workhorse in LV. No availability history to lean on, so the projection carries all the weight; rookie variance applies.

brief.prose: The bell-cow role is confirmed and the efficiency is not. He has cleared 20 touches in all three games, hit a season-high 84 percent snap share in Week 3 at New Orleans, and caught three balls for 37 yards in that game, but he is at 3.3 yards a carry for the season after 21 for 48 in Week 2 and 19 for 56 in Week 3, with Pro Football Focus grading the Raiders near the bottom of the league as a run-blocking unit and the guard spots the worst of it. He visited the trainers early in that Saints game and had both ankles taped, played all four quarters anyway, and turned up on Wednesday's Week 4 report as a full participant with an ankle listed. Volume this large survives bad weeks, so the role read is unchanged and the yards read is worse.
brief.rationale: Volume intact and still growing (84 percent of snaps, 20-plus touches every game) while efficiency has fallen to 3.3 YPC behind a bottom-tier run-blocking line; the Week 3 ankle taping cleared as full participation on Sept. 30.

events.headline: Commanders re-sign Austin Ekeler for depth; Rachaad White played through a shoulder injury
events.detail: Washington is signing Ekeler, pending a physical, back from the Achilles tear that ended his 2025 in Week 2. Team sources say the move was decided Saturday and is unrelated to Rachaad White's shoulder injury, which he suffered in the first half against Seattle before returning. The backfield is White (third downs, 151 scrimmage yards), Jacory Croskey-Merritt (team-high 142 rushing yards) and rookie Kaytron Allen.
events.so_what: Depth signing, not a role change: nobody in this backfield loses a lineup spot today. It does make the Washington committee even harder to start with confidence, and White's shoulder is the item to watch on the Wednesday report.

12534.name: Kyle Monangai

brief.prose: Chicago's second-year back in Ben Johnson's outside-zone scheme is the efficient half of a real two-man committee with D'Andre Swift, not a handcuff: he played 43% of the snaps in the Week 1 win at Carolina (12 touches, 124 yards, a rushing TD), then led the Bears in rushing in the Week 2 rain against Minnesota (10 for 47). Through two games he has 24 touches for 182 yards at 7.4 yards per carry, and Swift's fumble at the 1 in Week 2 gives him a case for more short-yardage work. The right knee that sent him to the medical tent against Minnesota and cost him Wednesday's practice is behind him for now: the Sun-Times reports he will play Monday against Philadelphia. The cap is the quarterback, with Caleb Williams out and Ben Johnson not yet choosing between Case Keenum and a Tyson Bagent who has not cleared the concussion protocol.
brief.rationale: The 43% committee half with elite efficiency, not a stash; knee cleared to play, but a backup QB caps Week 3.

13281.name: Jordyn Tyson

brief.prose: The plan for Moore and Nussmeier's offense was Tyson as a downfield weapon opposite Chris Olave, but an Aug. 13 hamstring strain (joint practice vs Jacksonville) has put real time on the shelf, with NFL Media pegging recovery at roughly two months and the team acknowledging he could open on IR (a minimum four-game absence). Moore blamed a foot-slip rather than a recurrence, but this is Tyson's fourth hamstring issue in four years. New Orleans has worked out Chase Claypool and Josh Reynolds as insurance. For redraft this is a fade: he misses the opening month, so he's a bench stash for later upside, not an early-season contributor.
brief.rationale: Two-month hamstring with possible IR; a redraft fade who misses the opening month, worth only a bench stash for later upside.

brief.prose: Arizona is running a true rotation, not a lead-back handoff: in the opener Tyler Allgeier out-snapped rookie Jeremiyah Love 44-32 (NBC's box score has it 41-32) and out-touched him 19-13, with Love getting 11 carries for 41 yards and a first-drive touchdown, plus two catches for 9 yards, and Allgeier taking the clock-killing work. Head coach Mike LaFleur said game flow drove the split and that Love was not on a snap count, then on Sept. 18 said the two 'are going to rotate' and that he would not call it an expanded role for Love in Week 2 against Seattle. The ankle is no longer the story (he is off the injury report), so the ceiling now depends on whether the hot-hand approach tilts toward the third overall pick as his conditioning builds; until touch counts move, treat this as a committee with the higher upside on Love's side.
brief.rationale: The head coach says the split is a rotation with no expanded role coming, which a board that prices Love as the lead back has probably not absorbed.
